newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Key Brazil state reports 790,000 tn soy crop loss.
newsitem.headline: Key Brazil state reports 790,000 tn soy crop loss.

text.p: Brazil's key soybean growing state of Rio Grande do Sul will see an irreversible crop loss of 790,854 tonnes this year because of drought, representing a loss of 200 million reais ($190 million), cooperative federation Fecotrigo said.
The state's 1996/97 crop was now expected to be less than 5.0 million tonnes, compared to an initial forecast of 5.7 million tonnes, Fecotrigo said in a statement.

"Until now, 55 percent of the total crop has been harvested, corresponding to 1.6 million hectares, registering an already irreversible loss of 25 percent -- with productivity of 1,479 kilos per hectare -- for a total (loss) of 790,854 tonnes," it said.

The remaining 45 percent of the crop to be harvested was mostly planted in December and could show an even higher percentage of losses as the dry weather in March struck during the key pod-filling phase of the crop, the federation said.
Productivity was initially expected to be 1,973 kilos per hectare.
Fecotrigo president Rui Polidoro Pinto will ask authorities to postpone the deadline for debt repayments for farmers affected by the drought, it said.
